name: TRex
what_it_is: TRex is a DPDK-based open-source traffic generator supporting stateless, stateful, and advanced stateful (ASTF) modes capable of generating L2-L7 traffic at up to 200 Gbps line rate. It provides a Python API, interactive console, and GUI for scripting realistic application traffic against network devices under test.
components: TRex server (DPDK data plane, JSON-RPC2 control plane)
TRex EMU (client-side L3 protocol emulation engine, 3-5 Mpps per thread)
BIRD routing daemon integration (BGP, OSPF, RIP, RPKI)
protocols: RPKI (ipv4, ipv6, vpn4, vpn6, multicast, flow4, flow6)
measurement: Per-stream and per-interface throughput statistics (hardware and software counters)
PCAP file transmission up to 1 TB for DPI testing
NAT/PAT dynamic translation learning and validation
configuration: Field engine: dynamic per-packet field modification (e.g., src_ip ranges, port ranges)
Variable packet sizes: 64 bytes to 9 KB (jumbo frames)
Rate specification: Mpps, L1 bandwidth, L2 bandwidth, or link percentage
Multiple simultaneous application profiles (HTTP, Citrix, etc.)
User-Agent field modification for L7 traffic
Up to 10,000 parallel streams in STL mode
BIRD routing profile injection (millions of routes in seconds)
fault_injection: Arbitrary/malformed packet construction via Scapy field engine
Cross-flow protocol fault support (limited; e.g., RTSP/SIP noted explicitly)
TCP SYN sequence randomization for connection tracking stress
modes: Stateless (STL): packet-based L2-L4 generation for routing/switching benchmarks, 10-30 Mpps per core
Stateful (STF): connection-aware traffic with L7 application profiles for firewall/IPS/NAT testing
Advanced Stateful (ASTF): full TCP/UDP emulation with L7 application layer for realistic flow behavior
EMU mode: client-side L3 protocol simulation (ARP, DHCP, ND, IGMP, BGP via BIRD)
Interactive mode: real-time console control and stream injection
Automated mode: Python API scripted runs
constraints: Requires DPDK-compatible NIC; physical interfaces must be bound to DPDK (kernel driver bypassed)
Supported NIC vendors: Intel, Mellanox, Broadcom, Cisco VIC, Napatech, Amazon ENA; not all NICs are supported
Runs on x86 or ARM server platforms only
Concurrent flow capacity is memory-limited (not CPU-limited)
ASTF TCP implementation is a pragmatic approximation, not a full kernel-grade TCP stack
Cross-flow L7 protocol support is limited to specific protocols (e.g., RTSP, SIP mentioned as partial)
No native HTTP/2 or gRPC protocol-specific stacks
Cluster/horizontal scaling mode is limited to controller tests, not general-purpose multi-node generation
Python client requires Python 2.7 or 3.x with specific library dependencies
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml found in the repository (deployment is bare-metal or VM via DPDK NIC binding)
No native HTTP/2 or gRPC protocol stacks
No full kernel-grade TCP stack (ASTF is a pragmatic approximation)
No general horizontal scaling across multiple TRex nodes for traffic generation
No built-in GUI dashboard for live metrics (requires separate console or third-party integration)
